title: Message family definitions
description: Meta-schema for schema/families.json. A family is a set of messages that draw their command values from one numbering and share the header that precedes a body. A channel carries one family, and schema/channels.json says which.

name.description: How a channel refers to this family.

header.description: What precedes a message body, in order, starting at the first byte of the payload. Every message of this family carries it, so no message repeats it among its own fields.

command.description: Which header field carries the value identifying a message, and which carries it where the first is a reserved escape. A family whose header carries no command has one message each way on each of its channels, which its revisions number 0.

escape.description: The value of that field which means the identifier is carried elsewhere.

extendedField.description: Which header field carries the identifier when the escape is present.

reserved.description: Values of the command field that introduce framing rather than identify a message of their own.
